name: Avatar Scenario
tagline: Build approved, accessible, avatar-led experiences with accountable human oversight on Azure.
customer_outcome: Audiences receive a clear, inclusive avatar-led experience while owners can trace each published claim to approved content, human approvals, responsible-AI disclosure, and operational evidence.
decision_prompts: Which Azure/Microsoft experience capability (Speech avatar batch, real-time avatar, Voice Live, video translation, or plain audio) fits the pilot's consent, accessibility, latency, language, and cost requirements?
Which communication, learning, or support moment, audience, locale, and channel should the pilot serve first?
Which approved sources and named owners may support the script, and when do they expire?
Who must approve factual accuracy, legal/compliance, brand, and accessibility before anything is published?
How will the experience disclose synthetic/AI assistance, offer human help, and avoid deceptive representation?
Which evaluation, red-team, and operational measures decide whether to iterate, scale, pause, or withdraw?

lessons.title: Module 2 — Provision the Foundry + Speech foundation
Module 3 — Build the governed content pipeline
Module 4 — Build the grounded assistant behind the experience
Module 5 — Generate the accessible avatar experience
Module 6 — Gate publication behind human approval
Module 7 — Evaluate, red-team, trace, and operate

build_modules.title: Verify and select the Azure experience capability
build_modules.summary: Before implementation, use current Microsoft docs to confirm a supported Speech avatar (batch or real-time), Voice Live, video-translation, or plain-audio capability, and record its API, region, identity, pricing, accessibility, content-safety, consent, and responsible-AI gating contract.
build_modules.checkpoint: Dated, evidence-backed capability decision record covering service, API, region, identity, pricing, accessibility, disclosure, and limited-access gating

build_modules.title: Provision the shared Foundry + Speech foundation
build_modules.summary: Deploy the keyless Foundry, model, Azure AI Search, Speech data plane, and observability baseline the avatar experience uses, with managed-identity RBAC and no secrets.
build_modules.checkpoint: Foundations Steps 1 and 2 plus a keyless .env contract

build_modules.title: Build the governed content pipeline
build_modules.summary: Connect approved source content, preserve owner/version/expiry metadata and access controls, and produce the typed, traceable claim set that gates everything downstream.
build_modules.checkpoint: Versioned claim set with authoritative sources, owners, and expiry

build_modules.title: Build the grounded assistant behind the experience
build_modules.summary: Build the model or Foundry agent path for cited drafting, refusal on unapproved claims, human escalation, and approved-content retrieval that feeds the script.
build_modules.checkpoint: Foundations Steps 3 and 4 — grounded, citing, refusing agent

build_modules.title: Generate the accessible avatar experience
build_modules.summary: Integrate the verified Speech capability with synthetic-media disclosure, transcript/captions, locale handling, and a non-avatar fallback, rendered only from an approved script revision.
build_modules.checkpoint: Accessible experience generated from an approved revision, with disclosure and fallback

build_modules.title: Gate publication behind human approval
build_modules.summary: Version output, collect factual, legal, brand, and accessibility approvals, and implement pause or withdrawal when a source changes.
build_modules.checkpoint: Approved publication and withdrawal record with a full trace

build_modules.title: Evaluate, red-team, trace, and operate
build_modules.summary: Measure grounding, disclosure, accessibility, handoff, and defect behaviour; red-team the experience; trace it; and deploy a controlled pilot with a scorecard and release decision.
build_modules.checkpoint: Pilot scorecard, red-team result, trace review, and release decision
